procedural_notes: MAINTAINER_CUT = line 63; FENCE_RANGES = none (registry references expand at build); body region = lines 1–62. Registry prompt references will expand to full fenced blocks at build time; lead-in rules apply to current form.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 41:"Want it on the remote anyway? Ask Claude to push the branch." — Two sentences separated by question mark; rule requires one sentence with command verb. Rule 2 explicitly: "one sentence with command verb summarizing what prompt does."
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consolidate to one imperative sentence: "Ask Claude to push the branch to remote if you want it off this laptop." or "To push to remote, ask Claude to push the branch."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 59:"If Claude stalls and you want to see whether it picks itself back up, this nudge is phrased as encouragement and lands as a taunt:" — Lacks command verb (verbs are "is phrased" and "lands", both descriptive not imperative). Rule 2 requires lead-in to start with action verb like "Ask Claude."
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rewrite to action-oriented: "If the task stalls and you want a nudge, ask Claude to continue with encouragement." or "Ask Claude to nudge this long-running task if it stalls."

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 67:"Extracted from `run-the-first-experiment.md` § *Send the task off*, 2026-08-12..." — Hard-grep match on "extracted from" (listed in rule 3's grep list). Also contains date 2026- and documentary passage "The section ran as unbroken module prose carrying four prompts... Two things changed beyond re-chunking..." documenting what was extracted and edited.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Remove provenance/edit-history passage entirely, or rewrite to present-state only. Line already documents the material is from an earlier source; the detailed edit-history ("ran as", "two things changed") should go to git blame/commit message, not maintainer block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 69:"that transition was removed in the same edit" — Transition verb "was removed" per rule 3: "Any clause whose verb states a transition (relocated, moved, split, renamed, became, now X rather than Y, predates, since, used to, previously) = biography."
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Rewrite to present-tense state: "The 12 min this file owns is the budget for the send-off beat; module total is 105 min." (states current fact, not that a transition occurred).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 75:"moved here 2026-08-12 with the send-off beat; they used to sit in `walk-and-send-off.md`, which no longer performs this work" — Hard-grep match on date "2026-08-12" (rule 3 grep: `2026-`). Also contains transition verbs "moved" and "used to" and "no longer" which all signal biography.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Remove the origin phrase and rewrite failure-modes block to present-tense state: "**Failure modes and diagnostics** (indexed for M4 send-off):" instead of documenting that they were moved from elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to articles only, not exercises.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
Over-hedge detector.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to reference artifacts, not exercises.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
Watch out for planting jargon too early.
Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise does not include this block; rule applies only if block present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing.
A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single-file judgment; rule applies to multi-file sweeps only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
Earn every technical term on first use.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to Agents 101 only; file is AE101.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
Golden path only in body.
Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to module debrief structures, not exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule applies to simulations with Teacher Claude, not this exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
Inline links use target's title, never filename.
Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
Session / task / run split.
No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
No meta-ask when student has already decided.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print.
Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
Name the artifact, don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
The curriculum does not narrate itself.
